purpose: Editorial relevance review for the letter-by-letter food audit. Keys below already resolve to their own bounded BibTeX entries. Do not treat a class 4–6 flag as a bibliography-join error.

classes.2: direct constituent evidence relevant to the food

items.title: Blueberries
items.page_claim: Polyphenol-rich diets are discussed as supporting endogenous antioxidant networks; quercetin/flavonols contribute to blueberry antioxidant activity.
items.paper_is: Generic review of quercetin as antioxidant/nutraceutical; not a blueberry trial.
items.rationale: Quercetin occurs in blueberries, but Boots 2008 is a generic quercetin review rather than blueberry or berry-matrix evidence. Prefer blueberry anthocyanin/flavonoid trials already on the page (Hein, Neshatdoust) or a blueberry-quercetin composition source.

items.title: Blueberries
items.page_claim: Polyphenol-rich diets supporting endogenous antioxidant networks (paired with Boots as [5,7]).
items.paper_is: Overview of the antioxidants and pro-antioxidants network; not blueberry-specific.
items.rationale: Generic antioxidant-network review. Does not evidence blueberry phenolics, anthocyanins, or blueberry feeding studies.

items.title: Carrots
items.page_claim: Carotenoids and cognitive/visual function context on a carrot page whose dominant carotenoid is β-carotene.
items.paper_is: Narrative review of lutein and zeaxanthin in visual and cognitive function across the lifespan; not a carrot study.
items.rationale: Johnson 2014 is a general lutein/zeaxanthin review. Carrots are not a primary lutein/zeaxanthin food. Food-specific carrot carotenoid evidence (mainly β-carotene, food-matrix fat co-ingestion) would be more appropriate.

items.title: Carrots
items.page_claim: Pair carrots with olive oil, avocado, or other fats in salads and cooked dishes.
items.paper_is: Mechanism of chylomicron formation and secretion; not carrot or salad evidence.
items.rationale: Same generic chylomicron mechanism used on corn and sesame. The pairing claim is preparation/matrix; Kindel does not study carrots. Included because the annotation was already a same-page sentence (not a neighbour-borrow) but the paper remains generic.
items.note: Not one of the 18 neighbour-borrow repairs; queued for the same scientific-relevance pattern.

items.title: Carrots
items.page_claim: Carotenoids implicated in neuroprotective antioxidant networks; fat co-ingestion implied.
items.paper_is: Carotenoid bioavailability from salads with full-fat vs fat-reduced dressings.
items.rationale: Genuine food-matrix fat–carotenoid evidence, but the matrix is salad dressing, not carrot-specific. Stronger than Kindel; still not carrot feeding evidence. Not one of the 18 neighbour-borrow repairs.

items.title: Corn
items.class_label: direct constituent evidence relevant to the food
items.page_claim: Corn lutein/zeaxanthin associated with cognitive performance.
items.paper_is: Narrative lutein/zeaxanthin review across the lifespan; not a corn trial.
items.rationale: Corn is a relevant lutein/zeaxanthin food, so the constituent is on-target, but the paper is still a generic review rather than corn-specific evidence. Yagi 2021 on the same page is closer to intake–cognition trials.

items.title: Corn
items.page_claim: Fat co-ingestion for carotenoid absorption (implied by reference list; not stated beside [5] in Overview).
items.paper_is: Mechanism of chylomicron formation and secretion.
items.rationale: Generic chylomicron physiology. Does not study corn, maize lutein, or a corn-containing meal.

items.title: Corn
items.page_claim: Carotenoid bioavailability with dietary fat.
items.paper_is: Salad carotenoid bioavailability with full-fat vs fat-reduced dressings; not corn.
items.rationale: Food-matrix fat effect on carotenoids, but the studied foods are salads/dressings. Borderline class 3; classified 4 because the page uses it as a generic absorption mechanism for corn.

items.title: Flax Seeds
items.class_label: direct constituent evidence relevant to the food
items.page_claim: ALA is useful but not a direct DHA/EPA source because conversion in humans is limited.
items.paper_is: NIH ODS omega-3 fact sheet for health professionals (web resource).
items.rationale: Correctly resolved. Relevant to flax ALA conversion limits, but it is a generic omega-3 fact sheet rather than flax feeding evidence. Optional later swap for a flax-seed or ALA-conversion primary paper.

items.title: Garlic
items.page_claim: Highlights currently attach [1] to garlic allicin/prebiotic bullets as well as the garlic-and-lemon lipid trial title.
items.paper_is: RCT of a garlic and lemon juice mixture on lipid profile in moderate hyperlipidaemia.
items.rationale: Direct food-intervention evidence, but it is a garlic-plus-lemon mixture, not garlic alone, and Highlights also use [1] for allicin/prebiotic claims the trial does not test. Keep the key; review claim-to-citation attachment in the letter audit. Do not edit Overview in the mechanical repair.

items.title: Garlic
items.class_label: direct constituent evidence relevant to the food
items.page_claim: Allicin chemistry, crushing, and glutathione-related sulfur compounds.
items.paper_is: Review of allicin chemistry and biological properties.
items.rationale: Correctly resolved and on-target for garlic’s characteristic constituent. Not food-intake evidence.

items.title: Herring
items.page_claim: Oily-fish EPA/DHA and cognitive/cardiometabolic context.
items.paper_is: RCT of DHA supplementation (capsule) and memory/reaction time in healthy young adults; not herring.
items.rationale: DHA supplement trial used where herring-as-food or oily-fish intake evidence would be more appropriate. McNamara 2006 on the same page is also generic omega-3 neurobiology.

items.title: Lamb
items.page_claim: Pair lamb with allium vegetables (onions, garlic, leeks) in stews and roasts.
items.paper_is: Garlic and onions cancer-prevention review; does not study lamb.
items.rationale: Correct key, wrong food. The papers evidence Allium cancer-prevention chemistry, not lamb. Citation supports a recipe pairing, not lamb composition or lamb feeding outcomes. Letter audit should not treat this as lamb evidence.

items.title: Lamb
items.page_claim: Pair lamb with allium vegetables to add sulfur-containing compounds and polyphenols.
items.paper_is: Bioactive S-alk(en)yl cysteine sulfoxide metabolites in Allium; does not study lamb.
items.rationale: Same recipe-context pattern as Nicastro: Allium chemistry cited on a lamb page because the suggested stew includes garlic/onions.

items.title: Lemon
items.page_claim: Overview attaches [1,2] to citrus flavanones (eriocitrin, hesperidin) and cardiometabolic relevance.
items.paper_is: RCT of garlic and lemon juice mixture on lipid profile; not a flavanone pharmacokinetic study.
items.rationale: Lemon juice is a study food, so this is direct mixture-trial evidence. The attached Overview claim is about citrus flavanones, which [2] Gimenez-Bastida actually addresses. Letter audit should split claims rather than drop the key blindly.

items.title: Saffron
items.page_claim: Saffron for depression — neurotransmitter, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective mechanisms.
items.paper_is: Comparative review of saffron as a therapeutic agent in depression.
items.rationale: Correctly resolved and on-target for saffron. The previous annotation was a dairy-calcium neighbour borrow (Soerensen); the paper itself is relevant. Included so the letter audit does not re-open a join error.

items.title: Salmon
items.page_claim: Regular inclusion of salmon and other oily fish for omega-3 intakes associated with cardiometabolic and cognitive benefits.
items.paper_is: DHA supplementation RCT in healthy young adults; not salmon or fish-meal evidence.
items.rationale: Supplement-DHA cognition trial used where salmon or oily-fish intake evidence would be more appropriate.

items.title: Sardines
items.page_claim: Marine omega-3 intake from sardines.
items.paper_is: DHA supplementation RCT; not sardines.
items.rationale: Same supplement-vs-food gap as herring and salmon.

items.title: Sesame Seeds
items.page_claim: Sesame/tahini fat co-ingestion improves carotenoid and fat-soluble vitamin absorption.
items.paper_is: Mechanism of chylomicron formation and secretion; not sesame or tahini.
items.rationale: Generic chylomicron mechanism used to underwrite a sesame pairing claim. Does not evidence sesame, tahini, or a sesame-containing meal.

items.title: Sesame Seeds
items.page_claim: Dietary fat effects on carotenoid bioavailability when pairing sesame with vegetables.
items.paper_is: Salad carotenoid bioavailability with full-fat vs fat-reduced dressings; not sesame.
items.rationale: Generic carotenoid-absorption matrix study (salads/dressings). Sesame is the proposed fat source, not the studied food. Borderline class 3.
